title: Exterior product in cohomology with closed support
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $A$ a finite commutative ring, and $X,Y$ schemes [def-pc-scheme] separated and of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ and $j:W\hookrightarrow Y$ be closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Put $P=X\times_kY$, with projections $p:P\to X$, $q:P\to Y$, and $h=i\times_kj:Z\times_kW\hookrightarrow P$ [def-pc-base-change]. On affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}B\subset X$ and $\operatorname{Spec}C\subset Y$, if $Z$ and $W$ are cut out by $I\subset B$ and $J\subset C$, the product immersion is cut out by the surjection $B\otimes_k C\to(B/I)\otimes_k(C/J)$ with kernel $I\otimes_k C+B\otimes_k J$. This also identifies its complement with the union of the inverse images of the two open complements. Work on small representatives of the small etale sites in the universe of [def-weil-size-convention], with ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $L\in D^+(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ suppose that
$$F=K\boxtimes_A^L L:=p^{-1}K\otimes_A^Lq^{-1}L$$
is bounded below; the inverse image and derived tensor are those of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-kun-derived-tensor]. Use the module-valued kernel-of-restriction and its derived functor [def-pur-etale-derived-supported-sections], whose cohomology is [def-pur-support-cohomology]. The supported exterior product is the following specified morphism in the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]:
$$
\kappa^{Z,W}_{K,L}:R\Gamma_Z(X,K)\otimes_A^LR\Gamma_W(Y,L)
\longrightarrow R\Gamma_{Z\times_kW}(P,F).
$$

Here is an explicit construction of the map. For any of the closed immersions $a:D\hookrightarrow T$ above, with open complement $v:V\hookrightarrow T$, and any $A$-module $M$, put
$$C_a(M)=a_*\underline M_D,\qquad e_a:\underline M_T\longrightarrow C_a(M),$$
where the constant sheaf is [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], the direct image is [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], and $e_a$ is the inverse-image/direct-image unit with the constant inverse-image identification. Equivalently, $e_a$ is the cokernel of $v_!\underline M_V\to\underline M_T$ in the module open-closed sequence [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact]. The constant-sheaf adjunction is the sheafification universal property: a map $\underline M_T\to G$ is a map $M\to\Gamma(T,G)$. The cokernel description and the extension-by-zero adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] therefore give
$$\operatorname{Hom}_T(C_a(M),G)=\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,\Gamma_D(T,G)).$$
Fix this adjunction by requiring that precomposition with $e_a$ is the constant-sheaf adjoint of the inclusion $\Gamma_D(T,G)\hookrightarrow\Gamma(T,G)$.

The stalks of $C_a(M)$ are $M$ on $D$ and zero off $D$: apply the finite stalk formula [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula], closed immersions being finite [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite], and [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk]. Exact stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] and their conservativity [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] thus make $C_a$ exact. The identical stalk argument makes $M\mapsto\underline M_T$ exact, so the quotient map $e_a$ also descends termwise to derived categories. Apply it termwise to complexes. The total right derived functor of $\Gamma_D$ is computed on K-injective resolutions by [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist, lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]; on bounded-below objects use the injective representatives of [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. Since $C_a$ is exact, [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors] gives the adjunction $C_a:D(A)\rightleftarrows D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A):R\Gamma_D$, with $C_a$ the left adjoint. Denote its evaluation counit by $\epsilon_a$. As a left adjoint, $C_a$ preserves direct sums, so its termwise application commutes with the direct sums in total tensor complexes.

For modules $M,N$, define
$$\theta_{M,N}:C_h(M\otimes_A N)\longrightarrow p^{-1}C_i(M)\otimes_Aq^{-1}C_j(N)$$
by factoring the constant-section tensor map followed by $p^{-1}e_i\otimes q^{-1}e_j$ through $e_h$. Sheaf tensor is [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. This factorization is unique: its target is zero on each of $(X\setminus Z)\times_kY$ and $X\times_k(Y\setminus W)$, whose union is the complement of $Z\times_kW$, so the map kills the open-extension term in the cokernel defining $e_h$. Extend $\theta$ to direct-sum total complexes by its map on each bidegree $(r,s)$ summand, with differential $d\otimes1+(-1)^r1\otimes d$. Uniqueness of the quotient factorization makes $\theta$ natural in both modules: both composites for a module map agree after precomposition with the epimorphism $e_h$. In particular $\theta_{r+1,s}C_h(d_M\otimes1)=(p^{-1}C_i(d_M)\otimes1)\theta_{r,s}$ and $\theta_{r,s+1}C_h(1\otimes d_N)=(1\otimes q^{-1}C_j(d_N))\theta_{r,s}$; adding the latter with coefficient $(-1)^r$ proves compatibility with the total differential.

Use K-flat resolutions to derive this comparison. The needed compatibility is checked directly on geometric stalks: $C_a(Q)$ has stalk $Q$ or zero, and exact inverse image has stalk the corresponding original stalk [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact, lem-weil-pbc-global-sections-stalk-comparison]. For a K-flat complex $Q$ of $A$-modules and an acyclic sheaf complex $E$, every stalk of $C_a(Q)\otimes_AE$ is $Q\otimes_A E_{\bar t}$ or zero, hence acyclic. Here tensor commutes with stalks by [lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar]. Its fixed-$A$ tensor and the tensor over the constant sheaf $A_T$ agree: sections of $A_T$ are locally represented by elements of $A$, so the two balancing relations agree after sheafification. Geometric stalks commute with direct sums, since the stalk is a filtered colimit of sections and sheafification does not change stalks; hence the same tensor formula holds for direct-sum total complexes. Exact conservative stalks detect acyclicity degree by degree. When each $Q^r$ is flat over $A$, these stalk formulas also show that tensoring any monomorphism of sheaves with $C_a(Q^r)$, or its inverse image, is injective on every stalk and hence is a monomorphism. Thus the resulting complexes have flat terms as required by the cited localization statement. Thus these coefficient complexes, and their inverse images, are K-flat. Resolutions exist by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], applied also to the one-point site for $A$-modules. The two-variable localization of K-flat complexes [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] consequently gives the specified derived comparison
$$\theta^L_{M,N}:C_h(M\otimes_A^LN)\longrightarrow p^{-1}C_i(M)\otimes_A^Lq^{-1}C_j(N),\qquad M,N\in D(A).$$

Writing $M=R\Gamma_Z(X,K)$ and $N=R\Gamma_W(Y,L)$, define $\kappa^{Z,W}_{K,L}$ to be the adjoint, under $C_h\dashv R\Gamma_{Z\times_kW}$, of
$$C_h(M\otimes_A^LN)\xrightarrow{\theta^L_{M,N}}p^{-1}C_i(M)\otimes_A^Lq^{-1}C_j(N)
\xrightarrow{p^{-1}\epsilon_i\otimes_A^Lq^{-1}\epsilon_j}p^{-1}K\otimes_A^Lq^{-1}L.$$
This specifies pulling back and tensoring supported sections, derived with K-flat tensor and injective support resolutions, without requiring $M\otimes_A^LN$ to be bounded below. Its composite with forgetting the output support is the ordinary exterior product [def-kun-kunneth-map] for $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ after forgetting both input supports, where $D((\operatorname{Spec}k)_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ is identified with $D(A)$ by the exact global-sections equivalence $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}k,-)$ [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk]; under it $Rf_*K$ for the structure map $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ becomes $R\Gamma(X,K)$, since $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}k,f_*I)=\Gamma(X,I)$ for a K-injective representative $I$, and the constant-sheaf functor becomes the inverse image along $f$: indeed, precomposing the displayed adjoint with $e_h$ replaces $\theta$ by $p^{-1}e_i\otimes q^{-1}e_j$, and the normalization of the three adjunctions replaces their counits by the ordinary evaluation maps. Deriving preserves this equality of natural maps by the same K-flat localization. Its cohomology groups use the support functors of [def-pur-support-cohomology].

proof.text: Prove supported-coefficient exactness using the exact constant-sheaf and closed-direct-image APIs. The unit for a closed immersion is epic: its cokernel restricts to zero on both the closed and open parts, hence vanishes. Therefore the coefficient quotient is epic.

proof.text: Identify global sections of the sheaf of supported sections with the kernel of restriction. Compose the constant-sheaf/global-sections adjunction on the closed scheme with the closed-direct-image/exceptional-inverse-image adjunction and transport through this kernel isomorphism. The terminal-object global-sections comparison gives the required quotient normalization; epimorphic quotients determine the counit and hence the adjunction uniquely.

proof.text: The fibre-product map of the two closed immersions is closed. The ordinary tensor target vanishes off the product support by the open-closed detection theorem and geometric-point factorization. Factor the constant tensor map uniquely through the closed quotient. Epimorphic quotient cancellation proves naturality in both module variables.

proof.text: Package the ordinary pairing as a bifunctor natural transformation. Apply HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctorComparison to construct its signed total-complex map. The map on each summand is the ordinary pairing followed by the target summand inclusion; preservation of coproducts and summand extensionality give uniqueness.

proof.text: Closed direct image preserves flatness by the open-closed partition of geometric points, the inverse-image/point comparison, and conservativity. Thus the second projected coefficient functor preserves flat objects. Functorial flat resolutions produce a left derivability structure for complexes whose second image is K-flat. The tensor localization counit is invertible on these models, so the existing two-variable localization universal property gives the unique natural derived comparison with its equation on every complex model. Retain the signed-total eqToHom localization factor explicitly and form the original adjoint exterior product from the two evaluation counits.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $Z\subset X,W\subset Y$ be closed subschemes of
separated finite-type
schemes over an algebraically closed field $k$. Fix a finite
commutative coefficient ring $A$, and let $K,L$ be bounded-below
complexes of $A$-module sheaves on their etale sites whose
derived exterior product
is bounded below. The *supported exterior product* is the map

$$
\kappa^{Z,W}_{K,L}:
R\Gamma_Z(X,K)\otimes_A^LR\Gamma_W(Y,L)
\longrightarrow
R\Gamma_{Z\times W}(X\times_kY,K\boxtimes_A^L L).
$$

It is obtained by pulling back sections in the two factors and
tensoring them: their supports meet in $Z\times W$.
Derive this pairing with K-flat tensor and injective support
resolutions.

Its composition with the map forgetting support is the ordinary exterior
product.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q62-856b3850f (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery against the current blueprint main-20261015 sk-prop-an/def-pur-supported-exterior-product.md (order 2282), the older master version (order 1938) and the statements of all 32 cited nodes. The hypotheses match the source one for one: algebraically closed k, separated finite-type X and Y, closed Z and W, any finite commutative A, K and L bounded below with K⊠L bounded below, and the tensor source in unbounded D(A). Nothing is weakened. Construction checks: (1) the product immersion has kernel I⊗C+B⊗J, and its complement is the union of the two pulled-back opens. (2) C_a=a_*M_D with e_a the cokernel map from lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact (module clause), and Hom(C_aM,G)=Hom_A(M,Γ_D G) via lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction, with a normalization that fixes the bijection. (3) A closed immersion has geometric fibres that are one point or empty, so C_a has stalks M or 0 and is exact. The derived adjunction comes from lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors, with K-injective resolutions for RΓ_D, and on D+ this agrees with Stacks 09XP (etale-cohomology.tex section-cohomology-support). (4) θ factors uniquely because its target vanishes on (X∖Z)×Y and on X×(Y∖W). The naturality identities and the sign (−1)^r are correct. (5) Stalks show the coefficient complexes and their inverse images are K-flat with flat terms, so lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent applies. (6) The transpose has the correct target, and on sections it sends a⊗b to p*a⊗q*b. Forgetting support works by the mate of e_a. Edge cases tested: empty support, full support (gives the ordinary product, as used by lem-pur-kunneth-supported), Spec k, the zero ring, Z/2 over Z/4, nonreduced Z. There are no new nodes. The rg duplicate search found only the ordinary exterior tensors pur7710-*, which are not this map, and def-pur-proetale-supported-exterior-product, the pro-étale analogue, which cites this item. No SGA source is used, there is no cycle, and no tool_uses are needed. I added lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk (1), the global-sections equivalence, with the identifications Rf_*K↔RΓ(X,K) and constant sheaf↔f⁻¹, and added it to stmt_deps; only the statement and stmt_deps change.
